payout_quote: We are conducting a clinical research study for ages 18-65 to evaluate the safety and tolerability of a medication that is implanted in the upper thigh. The study requires a screening visit, 1 or 2, 3-day/2-night stays at the facility, 22 follow-up visits and the final visit to remove the medication. Qualified participants receive 24-hour doctor/nursing care at no cost, private room, complimentary meals, and compensation up to $8,350 for time and travel associated with the study. ... Compensation varies by study, time involved, and whether you complete all visits and procedures in the study.
steps: Open the CenExel JBR (formerly J.B.R) healthy-volunteer study page.
Apply and complete the screening visit.
Complete the 1 or 2 3-day/2-night stays, all 22 follow-up visits, and the final medication-removal visit.
Receive compensation up to $8,350 for time and travel associated with the study.
catches: You must qualify and pass screening; the listing covers adults ages 18-65 and IRB-approved risk standards; not everyone qualifies.
The $8,350 is an 'up to' ceiling; compensation varies by study, time involved, and whether you complete all visits and procedures.
Heavy schedule: 1-2 stays of 2 nights each plus 22 follow-up visits — one of the longest commitments in this lane.
The study involves a medication implanted in the upper thigh (a minor surgical procedure to insert and remove) plus its systemic effects — real medical risks.
You may withdraw at any time, but that may reduce compensation below the ceiling.
biggest_catch: Up to $8,350 requires a medication to be implanted in the thigh and surgically removed, 1-2 overnight stays, and 22 follow-up visits — a months-long commitment — and only if you qualify and complete every visit and procedure.
eligibility: Healthy adults ages 18-65; must pass screening; every study approved and monitored by an Institutional Review Board.
timing: Compensation paid for time and travel while participating in the study.
